## Why You’ll Love This Crispy Home Fries Recipe

*   **Potatoes: The Ultimate Comfort Food**. Potatoes are a key ingredient in many of our favorite comfort foods ([Mashed Potatoes](https://www.wellplated.com/mashed-potatoes-recipe/)! [Hashbrown Casserole](https://www.wellplated.com/hash-brown-casserole/)!), but if you want your potato fix without having to buy a bunch of other ingredients, home fries are ideal. This is a stripped down way to enjoy potatoes in their finest form: crispy on the outside, tender on the inside, and perfectly seasoned.
*   **Easy to Make****Potatoes**. While there _is_ some prep work involved, once that’s over, you’re mere minutes away from fried potato bliss. Truly, the hardest part is being patient enough to resist the urge to stir the potatoes so they get crispy.
*   **Fail-Proof Method**. If you’ve tried making home fries (or hash browns) in the past and struggled with them sticking to the pan, ending up mushy, or not cooking all the way through, this recipe will become your go-to. It really works! (Be sure to try these [Sweet Potato Hash Browns](https://www.wellplated.com/sweet-potato-hash-browns/) too.)

![Image 11: Breakfast home fries on plate with spoon](blob:http://localhost/659926dcafebe7d5f163fbc40297dcc3)
## How to Make Crispy Home Fries

### **The Ingredients**

*   **Yukon Gold Potatoes**. I think Yukon gold are the best potatoes for home fries because they have a fabulous buttery flavor and a texture that’s not too starchy, nor too waxy.
*   **Unsalted Butter**. Using unsalted butter puts you in control of the flavor. If you only have salted butter on hand, you can use that, but dial back the added kosher salt.
*   **Seasonings**. Paprika for color (either sweet or smoked will work here), freshly ground pepper if you’d like, and optional fresh chives, green onions, parsley, or cilantro.

## Market Swap

Although I like Yukon gold potatoes best, russet potatoes will also work for home fries. Don’t use a waxy potato like red potatoes, though—save them for [Roasted Red Potatoes](https://www.wellplated.com/roasted-red-potatoes/).

### The Directions

![Image 13: Home fries in skillet after adding butter](blob:http://localhost/b3e13bbba1514f9b569e5ae0202985f3)
1.   **Soak**. Let the potatoes sit in a bowl of hot water for 5 minutes. This is MANDATORY or the potatoes will stick to the skillet.

![Image 15: Home fries in skillet after adding butter](blob:http://localhost/b3e13bbba1514f9b569e5ae0202985f3)
1.   **Drain**. Pour the potatoes into a colander and rinse them with warm water.

![Image 17: Home fries in skillet after adding butter](blob:http://localhost/b3e13bbba1514f9b569e5ae0202985f3)
1.   **Dry**. Spread the potatoes onto a kitchen towel and pat them dry.

![Image 19: Home fries in skillet after adding butter](blob:http://localhost/b3e13bbba1514f9b569e5ae0202985f3)
1.   **Prepare**. Whisk the water, oil, and salt in a skillet.

![Image 21: Home fries in skillet after adding butter](blob:http://localhost/b3e13bbba1514f9b569e5ae0202985f3)
1.   **Add the Potatoes**. Make sure they’re in an even layer, then cover the skillet. Cook over medium heat for 5 minutes.

![Image 23: Home fries in skillet after adding butter](blob:http://localhost/b3e13bbba1514f9b569e5ae0202985f3)
1.   **Add the Butter**. Just a tablespoon for now! Once it melts, cover the pan and cook 2 minutes more.

![Image 25: Home fries in skillet after adding butter](blob:http://localhost/b3e13bbba1514f9b569e5ae0202985f3)
1.   **Crisp Them**. Uncover the skillet and cook for 5 minutes without disturbing. Stir in the rest of the butter and paprika, then cook in an even layer for 3 more minutes. Keep cooking, stirring every 2 to 3 minutes, until the home fries are crispy. Season with salt, pepper, and fresh herbs if you’re using them. ENJOY!

![Image 27: Breakfast home fries on plate with spoon](blob:http://localhost/659926dcafebe7d5f163fbc40297dcc3)
## Recipe Variations

*   **Home Fries With Onions**. For diner-style breakfast potatoes, dice a small onion and cook it in the skillet with oil before starting the potatoes; add them back in at the end of the cooking time.
*   **Spicy Home Fries**. Add cayenne pepper with the paprika.
*   **Home Fries With Peppers**. Add a half cup of diced bell peppers (any color you like) to the potatoes.

## What to Serve with Home Fries

*   **Eggs**. If savory breakfasts are your jam, serve these home fries with [Egg Muffins](https://www.wellplated.com/healthy-breakfast-egg-muffins/) or [Eggs in Purgatory](https://www.wellplated.com/eggs-in-purgatory/).
*   **Other Breakfast Foods**. For that sweet and savory contrast, pair potatoes with [Fluffy Pancakes](https://www.wellplated.com/fluffy-pancakes-for-dad-with-love/) or [Overnight French Toast](https://www.wellplated.com/overnight-french-toast/).
*   **Burgers**. Instead of [Potato Wedges](https://www.wellplated.com/air-fryer-potato-wedges/), sometimes I make a batch of crispy home fries in a skillet for pairing with[Salmon Burgers](https://www.wellplated.com/salmon-burgers/).
*   **Meat**. Anything you’d pair with roasted potatoes will go with home fries too! [Air Fryer Steak](https://www.wellplated.com/air-fryer-steak/), [Baked BBQ Chicken](https://www.wellplated.com/bbq-chicken/)—you get the idea.
*   **Ketchup**. Or hot sauce if you’re feelin’ spicy.

![Image 29: Breakfast home fries on plate with spoon](blob:http://localhost/659926dcafebe7d5f163fbc40297dcc3)
## Recipe Tips and Tricks

*   **Don’t Skip the Soaking and Drying**. Mushy potatoes that stick to the pan and break your potato-loving heart will be a thing of the past! 
*   **Skip the Boiling! Steam, then Fry**. This recipe’s process of cooking the potatoes in a little water in the pan, then letting the water cook off and frying is key to perfect home fries. The first part ensures that the potatoes are tender, while the second part gives them that crispy exterior, all without the fuss of boiling the potatoes first.
*   **Be Patient**. At three points in this recipe, you’ll need to cook the potatoes without disturbing them. This might make you antsy, but trust the process! If you stir the potatoes before they’re nicely browned, they’ll end up mushy and soft.
*   **Cook Bigger Batches Separately**. If you want to make home fries for a crowd, you’ll have to do it in separate batches rather than cooking all the potatoes at once. Crowding the pan will steam them, which isn’t what we want here.
*   **Don’t Hold Back on the Oil and Butter**. This, too, helps get the potatoes crispy and keeps them from sticking to the pan. (It also makes them delectable!)

### Ingredients

1x 2x 3x

*   1 pound Yukon gold potatoes scrubbed and cut into 1/2-inch cubes (about 2 medium; leave the peels on)
*   ⅓ cup water
*   2 tablespoons[canola oil](https://amzlink.to/az0DtL3ots6er)
*   1 teaspoon[kosher salt](https://amzlink.to/az00z26Z16DwJ)plus a few big pinches
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter divided
*   1 teaspoon[paprika](https://amzlink.to/az0VwRnfccJQt)
*   Freshly ground pepper optional
*   Sprinkle fresh chives, green onion, parsley, or cilantro optional

* * *

### Instructions

SHOW IMAGES

*   Place the potatoes in a large bowl and cover with hot water. Let sit 5 minutes, then drain in a colander; rinse further under running warm water, then drain, spread onto a clean kitchen towel, and pat dry (this step is annoying but will prevent your potatoes from sticking to the pan and making a hot mess). ![Image 35: Home fries in skillet after adding butter](blob:http://localhost/ccb98d875cf716fb3bf09b135468ca7a) 
*   In a 12-inch cast iron or similar heavy bottomed skillet, whisk together the water, oil, and salt. Add the potatoes in an even layer. Turn the stove heat to medium, cover the skillet (if your skillet does not have a cover, you can lay a sheet pan on top of it), and cook without disturbing for 5 minutes . Uncover, stir in 1 tablespoon of the butter until it melts, recover, and cook 2 minutes more. ![Image 37: Home fries in skillet after adding butter](blob:http://localhost/ccb98d875cf716fb3bf09b135468ca7a) 
*   Time to crisp! Uncover the skillet and let cook for 5 minutes without disturbing; some of the water will evaporate and the potatoes will begin to crisp. Stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon butter, then the paprika. Spread the potatoes back into an even layer and let cook 3 more minutes undisturbed. Continue cooking until the water has evaporated and the potatoes are crisp all over, about 6 minutes more, stirring every 2 to 3 minutes. Sprinkle with a few big pinches of salt salt and serve hot with pepper and chives to taste. ![Image 39: Home fries in skillet after adding butter](blob:http://localhost/ccb98d875cf716fb3bf09b135468ca7a) 

### Notes

*   **TO STORE**: Refrigerate leftover home fries in an airtight container for up to 4 days. I do not recommend freezing them; potatoes don’t freeze well.
*   **TO REHEAT**: Reheat leftovers in a non-stick skillet set over medium heat or in the microwave until warmed through.

If you know me, you know my love runs deep for [Sweet Potato Fries](https://www.wellplated.com/sweet-potato-fries/). But what you might not know is that I also have a soft spot in my heart for **yuca fries**.

When Ben was in the Peace Corps and I visited him in the Dominican Republic, I ate a ton of them.

*   They’ve got everything you love about fries—**crispy! fluffy! dippable!**—but I’d say the texture is even _better_.
*   Just like any [Homemade Fries](https://www.wellplated.com/baked-fries/), the flavor of yuca fries really comes from the seasoning. I like to use a savory combo of garlic and onion powder with paprika, but there are **endless seasoning options**. You can even make them sweet if you want!
*   Some recipes for yuca fries call for deep frying, but I’ve found that it’s not necessary—**baking in the oven** works just fine! (Honestly, my opposition to deep frying is more about the hassle and cleanup than anything else. And the smell! No thank you!)

## Key Ingredients

You’ll find the full list of ingredients in the recipe card below, but here are some notes to keep in mind.

*   **Yuca Root**. If you’ve never bought yuca before, it looks a little bit like an elongated, extra-craggly potato. Unfortunately, it’s not exactly a hot commodity at the grocery store, so it’s important to make sure it’s good before buying it—there shouldn’t be any cracks in the skin or any signs of mold.
*   **Seasonings**. Garlic powder, paprika, onion powder, and ground black pepper. You can use sweet paprika or smoked paprika for some smoky flavor.
*   **Garnishes**. If you’d like, you can sprinkle cilantro, chives, green onion, or parsley onto the yuca fries before serving.

## How to Make Yuca Fries

![Image 12: Overhead view of yuca fries on parchment-lined baking sheet](blob:http://localhost/b3e13bbba1514f9b569e5ae0202985f3)![Image 14: Overhead view of yuca fries on parchment-lined baking sheet](blob:http://localhost/b3e13bbba1514f9b569e5ae0202985f3)![Image 16: Overhead view of yuca fries on parchment-lined baking sheet](blob:http://localhost/b3e13bbba1514f9b569e5ae0202985f3)![Image 18: Overhead view of yuca fries on parchment-lined baking sheet](blob:http://localhost/b3e13bbba1514f9b569e5ae0202985f3)![Image 20: Overhead view of yuca fries on parchment-lined baking sheet](blob:http://localhost/b3e13bbba1514f9b569e5ae0202985f3)![Image 22: Overhead view of yuca fries on parchment-lined baking sheet](blob:http://localhost/b3e13bbba1514f9b569e5ae0202985f3)
**Prep the Yuca**. Start by peeling the yuca root, then trim the ends. There shouldn’t be any brown or purple streaks on the yuca root when you’re finished; these parts are fibrous and unpleasant to eat.

**Cut Fries**. Slice the root into the shape of fries.Make sure they’re cut into even sizes so they all finish cooking at the same time!

**Boil**. Cook the yuca fries in salted water until they’re tender but still firm.

**Dry**. Spread the boiled fries onto towels and pat dry.

**Season**. Toss the yuca with olive oil and the seasonings.

**Bake**. Spread the fries on a baking sheet in a single layer with space between each fry and bake in a 425 degree F oven for 15 minutes.

**Flip and Finish**. Turn the fries to get the other sides nicely browned and bake for 10 to 15 minutes more, or until crispy. Season the yuca fries with additional salt, add fresh herbs, and ENJOY!

## Recipe Variations

*   **Cheesy Yuca Fries**. After flipping the fries, sprinkle them with freshly grated Parmesan.
*   **Sweet Yuca Fries**. Instead of salt and spices, toss the yuca fries with cinnamon and sugar.These are delish with mole sauce!
*   **Spicy Yuca Fries**. Add cayenne pepper, chili powder, or chipotle powder to the seasoning mix.

*   ½ teaspoon[onion powder](https://amzlink.to/az05xDd0zLyQT)

### Instructions

SHOW IMAGES

*   Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Remove the tough, fibrous outside from the yuca: trim off the ends, then use a vegetable peeler to remove the skin entirely so no brown or purle streaks remain (you will probably need to run the peeler over it twice). If any parts stuck, stand the yuca up on a flat end and use a knife to carefully cut down along the sides, leaving no part of the brown, rough bits. ![Image 28: Overhead view of yuca fries on parchment-lined baking sheet](blob:http://localhost/ccb98d875cf716fb3bf09b135468ca7a) 
*   Cut the yuca into fry-shaped sticks that are about ¼- to ½-inch wide and 3-inches long. Make the yuca pieces as uniform as possible so that the fries bake evenly. ![Image 30: Overhead view of yuca fries on parchment-lined baking sheet](blob:http://localhost/ccb98d875cf716fb3bf09b135468ca7a) 
*   Add 1 tablespoon of salt to the water, then add the yuca. Boil for 8 minutes, until they are fork tender but not falling apart. Spread out onto a clean kitchen towel or paper towels, pat dry, and let continue to air dry for at least 15 minutes—the yuca will be very starchy. ![Image 32: Overhead view of yuca fries on parchment-lined baking sheet](blob:http://localhost/ccb98d875cf716fb3bf09b135468ca7a) 
*   Place racks in the lower and upper thirds of your oven and preheat the oven to 425°F. Line two large, rimmed baking sheets with parchment paper. Add the dried yuca to a large bowl. Drizzle with the oil. In a small bowl, combine the remaining 1 teaspoon salt, the garlic powder, paprika, onion powder, and black pepper. Sprinkle over the yuca, toss to evenly coat, then spread the yuca in a single layer on the prepared baking sheets, dividing it evenly so the fries are not touching. ![Image 34: Overhead view of yuca fries on parchment-lined baking sheet](blob:http://localhost/ccb98d875cf716fb3bf09b135468ca7a) 
*   Bake yuca fries on the upper and lower thirds for 15 minutes. Remove from the oven, use a spatula to flip, then return the pans to the oven, switching their positions on the upper and lower racks. Continue baking until the fries are golden and crisped to your liking, about 10 to 15 minutes more. Sprinkle immediately with a pinch of additional salt and cilantro or herbs of choice. ![Image 36: Overhead view of yuca fries on parchment-lined baking sheet](blob:http://localhost/ccb98d875cf716fb3bf09b135468ca7a)

*   **TO REHEAT**: Reheat the yuca fries in a 425ºF oven or air fryer until they’re warmed through.

Everyone loves fries, let’s be real. But **steak fries** are for people who don’t just love fries, but have a deep adoration for potatoes in all their forms.

*   While other fries are all about that **crispy, golden exterior**, steak fries also have a **creamy interior** going for them—kind of like [Oven Roasted Potatoes](https://www.wellplated.com/oven-roasted-potatoes/) in fry form.
*   They’re also bigger, which means you can scoop up more ketchup (or toppings, if you’re partial to [Chili Cheese Fries](https://www.wellplated.com/chili-cheese-fries/)) with each fry.
*   This steak fry recipe has my **favorite fry seasoning** blend, which combines sweet paprika with garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper. It’s savory, salty, and everything you want for steak fries!
*   Rather than deep frying in oil, these steak fries are **oven-baked**, which is lighter and easier. In the case of steak fries, baking actually gives you a better texture than deep frying. Double win!

Grab a bottle of ketchup, let’s dig in.

![Image 14: A plate of seasoned steak fries is served with a small bowl of ketchup and another bowl of a creamy dipping sauce on a light countertop. The wedges are golden and crispy, arranged neatly on a white plate.](blob:http://localhost/cf26e60dfda81ddb17d3f6bf63c29db5)
## What Are the Best Potatoes for Steak Fries?

You have two good options for making steak fries: Yukon gold or russet potatoes.

*   As you’ll see in the recipe card below, I use **Yukon gold potatoes**. I like them because they have a creamy interior and a natural buttery flavor. They’re also the perfect size for making fries!
*   **Russet potatoes** are starchier, so if you prefer the insides of your steak fries fluffy, they’re your best bet. You may have to cut the fries in half so they’re not unwieldy if your potatoes are especially large.

## How to Make Steak Fries

![Image 16: A baking sheet lined with parchment paper holds golden-brown steak fries, spread out evenly and seasoned, fresh out of the oven.](blob:http://localhost/b3e13bbba1514f9b569e5ae0202985f3)![Image 18: A baking sheet lined with parchment paper holds golden-brown steak fries, spread out evenly and seasoned, fresh out of the oven.](blob:http://localhost/b3e13bbba1514f9b569e5ae0202985f3)![Image 20: A baking sheet lined with parchment paper holds golden-brown steak fries, spread out evenly and seasoned, fresh out of the oven.](blob:http://localhost/b3e13bbba1514f9b569e5ae0202985f3)![Image 22: A baking sheet lined with parchment paper holds golden-brown steak fries, spread out evenly and seasoned, fresh out of the oven.](blob:http://localhost/b3e13bbba1514f9b569e5ae0202985f3)
**Prepare**. Line a sheet pan with parchment paper and pop it in the oven while it preheats to 450ºF.

**Cut Your Fries**. Slice them into wedges and place them in a bowl. I like leaving the skin on. Extra fiber and extra crispiness!

**Season the Fries**. Toss them in a bowl with oil and seasonings.

**Bake**. Place the steak fries on the preheated pan and bake for 20 minutes. Flip and cook for 15 to 20 minutes more, or until browned and crispy. Serve with a [Smash Burger](https://www.wellplated.com/smash-burger/), [Turkey Burger](https://www.wellplated.com/turkey-burgers/), or [Air Fryer Grilled Cheese](https://www.wellplated.com/air-fryer-grilled-cheese/). ENJOY!

## Recipe Variations

*   **Make Them Truffle Fries**. Truffle fries are usually thin and delicate, but steak fries give you more surface area for Parm and truffle oil. Use my recipe for [Truffle Fries](https://www.wellplated.com/truffle-fries/) as inspiration.
*   **Load Them Up**. Steak fries are perfect for making[Carne Asada Fries](https://www.wellplated.com/carne-asada-fries/) and [Chicken Bacon Ranch Fries](https://www.wellplated.com/chicken-bacon-ranch-fries/).
*   **Switch Up the Seasonings**. Fresh minced rosemary is always good with fries, as is Old Bay seasoning, especially if you’re serving them with [Air Fryer Fish](https://www.wellplated.com/air-fryer-fish/).

### Ingredients

1x 2x 3x

*   2 tablespoons[canola oil](https://amzlink.to/az0DtL3ots6er)or high temperature cooking oil of choice
*   4 medium Yukon gold potatoes about 1 pound, 6 ounces
*   2 teaspoons[paprika](https://amzlink.to/az0VwRnfccJQt)
*   1 ½ teaspoons[kosher salt](https://amzlink.to/az00z26Z16DwJ)
*   ½ teaspoon[garlic powder](https://amzlink.to/az0n2D8DyKZeG)
*   ¼ teaspoon[onion powder](https://amzlink.to/az05xDd0zLyQT)
*   ¼ teaspoon[ground black pepper](https://amzlink.to/az05YM4bVg4JE)

* * *

### Instructions

SHOW IMAGES

*   Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper. Place the pan in the center of the oven and preheat to 450°F. 
*   Scrub and dry the potatoes. Cut into wedges that are 1/2-inch wide at the thickest part. Transfer to a large bowl. ![Image 30: A baking sheet lined with parchment paper holds golden-brown steak fries, spread out evenly and seasoned, fresh out of the oven.](blob:http://localhost/ccb98d875cf716fb3bf09b135468ca7a) 
*   Toss the potatoes with the oil, paprika, salt, garlic powder, onion powder, and black pepper. ![Image 32: A baking sheet lined with parchment paper holds golden-brown steak fries, spread out evenly and seasoned, fresh out of the oven.](blob:http://localhost/ccb98d875cf716fb3bf09b135468ca7a) 
*   Once the oven is preheated, remove the baking sheet from the oven and spread the potatoes into a single layer. They can touch a bit at the sides but should not overlap. Roast for 20 minutes. ![Image 34: A baking sheet lined with parchment paper holds golden-brown steak fries, spread out evenly and seasoned, fresh out of the oven.](blob:http://localhost/ccb98d875cf716fb3bf09b135468ca7a) 
*   Remove the baking sheet from the oven and with a spatula, flip them over in big sections. Return to an even layer, then place the pan back in the oven and continue baking until the potatoes are golden and crisped to your liking, about 15 to 20 minutes more. Let cool a few minutes, then enjoy. ![Image 36: A baking sheet lined with parchment paper holds golden-brown steak fries, spread out evenly and seasoned, fresh out of the oven.](blob:http://localhost/ccb98d875cf716fb3bf09b135468ca7a) 

### Notes

*   You can swap russet potatoes, but I really feel like Yukon golds have the best crispy outside to creamy inside ratio. Because russet potatoes are larger, you may need to cut some of the fries in half prior to roasting to keep all of the pieces similar in size.
*   **TO STORE**: Place leftover steak fries in an airtight storage container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
*   **TO REHEAT**: You can reheat steak fries by preheating your oven to 400 degrees and placing an empty baking sheet in the oven _while the oven preheats._ Spread the leftover fries in a single layer on the hot pan, then pop the pan into the preheated oven for 5 to 8 minutes. Watch the fries carefully the last few minutes to make sure they do not burn.
